rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Moses answered that he was most learned; God corrected him and directed him to a servant at the meeting of the seas who knew more.
rows.anchor: فأوحى إليه بل أعلم منك عبد لي عند مجمع البحرين وهو الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was told to seek the servant at the shore by a rock, carrying salted fish in a basket; the fish's disappearance would mark the place.
rows.anchor: اطلبه على ساحل البحر عند الصخرة وخذ حوتا مملوحا في مكتل يكون زادا لك

rows.speaker: أهل التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah's people identify this Moses as Moses son of Misha son of Joseph, a prophet before Moses son of Imran, because they found it implausible for God's chosen interlocutor to learn from someone beneath him.
rows.anchor: وزعم أهل التوراة أن موسى هذا هو موسى بن ميشا بن يوسف النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fully learned person can still lack some knowledge; excellence is relative, and someone superior in one respect can be inferior in another.
rows.anchor: فلهذا لا يبعد عن العالم الكامل أن يجهل بعض الأشياء فالفاضل قد يكون مفضولا من وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The companion is Joshua son of Nun, Joseph's descendant and Moses's nephew; he later succeeded Moses in the law and was among Israel's foremost figures.
rows.anchor: وهو يوشع بن نون بن افراييم بن يوسف وهو ابن أخت موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fata can mean a servant or student even if elderly; Joshua is called this because he served, followed, and learned from Moses.
rows.anchor: ويسمى الخادم والتلميذ فتى وإن كان شيخا

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet taught people to say my young man or young woman instead of my slave or female slave.
rows.anchor: ليقل أحدكم فتاي وفتاتي ولا يقل عبدي وأمتي

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf says that calling oneself another person's fata amounts to admitting enslavement.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يوسف : من قال أنا فتى فلان كان إقرارا منه بالرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors identifying Moses with Moses son of Imran, the first of the two views just discussed; a journey with a companion of great stature befits him.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير المشهور وهو الوجه الأول وتأبى جلالة هذا السفر إلا أن يكون الصاحب من أولي الخطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La abrahu means I will keep going; its omitted predicate is understood from the travel context, also confirmed by the later mention of their journey.
rows.anchor: لا أزال أسير فحذف الخبر اعتمادا على قرينة الحال

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saadi al-Mufti says the Quran's wording does not indicate that Moses was already traveling; the author rejects this as overlooking the next verse's journey reference.
rows.anchor: فقول سعدي المفتي : لا دلالة في نظم القرآن على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting of the two seas is where the Persian and Roman seas nearly meet toward the east, the promised meeting place with Khidr.
rows.anchor: هو ملتقى بحر فارس والروم مما يلي المشرق وهو المكان الذي وعد الله موسى بلقاء الخضر فيه

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saadi says the Persian and Roman seas meet in the western ocean; the author replies that this refers to their actual confluence, while this verse means a nearby eastern place.
rows.anchor: بحرا فارس والروم إنما يلتقيان في المحيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In an inward reading, Moses and Khidr are two seas of knowledge: Moses is dominated by outward law and Khidr by inward truth; their meeting is their encounter.
rows.anchor: موسى بحر الظاهر والباطن والغالب عليه الظاهر على الشريعة والآخر وهو الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amda means to proceed in or carry through an affair.
rows.anchor: من مضى في الأمر بمعنى نفذ وأمضاه أنفذه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi has Moses ask Joshua to accompany him in seeking the righteous servant, and Joshua welcomes the valuable companionship.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (موسى عليه السلام فرمودكه اي يوشع توبامن موافقت نماى در طلب اين بنده صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa introduces an understood sequence: Moses and Joshua walked until they reached a place near the midpoint of the seas' lengthwise extension.
rows.anchor: والفاء فصيحة أي : فذهب موسى ويوشع يمشيان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: At the life-spring beside the rock, Moses slept; Joshua's ablution water fell on the roasted fish, reviving it so it moved into the sea, while Joshua was astonished.
rows.anchor: ويوشع دران شمه وضو ساخت وقطره برآن ماهى بريان كيد في الحال زنده شد روى بدريا نهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared wording that they forgot their fish does not conflict with sound reports assigning the actual forgetting to Joshua: Moses forgot to remind him, while Joshua forgot to tell him.
rows.anchor: نسي موسى تذكر الحوت لصاحبه وصاحبه نسي الأخبار بأمره فلا يخالفه ما في حديث الصحيحين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation says both had provision for the journey, so a shared verb can describe forgetting even when only one carried the fish, as people say a group took provisions when only some did.
rows.anchor: كانا جميعا قد زوداه لسفرهما فجاز إضافة ذلك إليهما وإن كان الناسي أحدهما وهو يوشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fa before the fish's path is explanatory, not necessarily coordinated with the forgetting; the implied sequence is that the fish revived, fell into the sea, and took its path.
rows.anchor: والتقدير وحيى الحوت فسقط في البحر فاتخذ

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explained the fish's path as a tunnel-like passage beneath water held back over it like an arch.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى أمسك جرية الماء على الحوت فصار كالطاق عليه

rows.speaker: ابن ملك
rows.claim: Ibn Malik says ara'ayta can mean tell me; here it expresses amazement, with its object omitted and supplied by the recollection of arriving at the rock.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن ملك هو يجيىء بمعنى أخبرني وهنا بمعنى التعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joshua says he forgot to tell Moses about the fish and its marvel; Satan distracted him, and remembering earlier would have prevented them passing the place and suffering fatigue.
rows.anchor: لموسى ما جاوز ذلك المكان وما ناله النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an adhkurahu is an explanatory supplement to the pronoun; ajaban is the second object of ittakhadha, describing the fish's tunnel-like route.
rows.anchor: أي : وما أنساني أن أذكره لك

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam asks how Joshua could forget a marvelous sign, then answers that frequent miracles from Moses may have made this one less striking to him.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام : فإن قيل انقلاب السمكة المالحة حية حالة عجيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author offers another answer: God removed Joshua's necessary recollection so Moses would learn that knowledge depends on God's teaching and preservation of thoughts.
rows.anchor: وعندي فيه جواب آخر وهو أن موسى لما استعظم علم نفسه أزال الله تعالى عن قلب صاحبه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say Joshua forgot because he was absorbed in witnessing the miraculous revival and movement of the salted fish and the water; he blamed Satan to humble himself.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لعله نسي ذلك لاستغراقه في الاستبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recognizes the fish's disappearance as the sign they sought because it marked the way to meeting Khidr; they retrace their path carefully to the rock.
rows.anchor: نبغيه ونطلبه لكونه أمارة للفوز بالمرام من لقاء الخضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They returned from the river mouth to follow their tracks, inspecting them closely until they reached the rock where the fish entered its tunnel.
rows.anchor: رجعا من ذلك الموضع وهو طرف نهر ينصب إلى البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qasasan is an implied verbal noun: they followed their tracks and examined them closely.
rows.anchor: يتبعان آثارهما اتباعا ويتفحصان تفحصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite servant signals exaltation, and the possessive phrase from Our servants confers honor; Moses greets Khidr, identifies himself, and says he came to learn.
rows.anchor: وكان مسجى بثوب فسلم عليه موسى وعرفه نفسه

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority identify the servant as Khidr, whose title, according to a sound report, came from sitting on barren white ground that turned green behind him.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنه الخضر بفتح الخاء المعجمة وكسر الضاد وهو لقبه

rows.speaker: أبو الليث
rows.claim: Abu al-Layth relates that Khidr was a king's son who refused succession, fled his father, and escaped to the sea islands.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الليث : إنه عليه السلام ذكر قصة الخضر

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli's account says Khidr's father was a king, his mother a Persian princess, and he was born in a cave and nursed by a village shepherd's goat before being raised by the shepherd.
rows.anchor: أن أباه كان ملكا وأن أمه كانت بنت فارس واسمها إلها وإنها ولدته في مغارة

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: In that account, Khidr later came to his father's court as a scribe; his father recognized him, appointed him over the people, but Khidr eventually fled and renounced worldly life.
rows.anchor: كان فيمن قدم عليه من الكتاب ابنه الخضر وهو لا يعرفه فلما استحسن خطه ومعرفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Khidr could not remain alive because no prophet follows Muhammad fails: Khidr was a prophet before Muhammad, and God preserved him for a wisdom as with Jesus.
rows.anchor: فلا عبرة لكلامه لأنه لم يتنبأ بعده بل قبله كعيسى أبقاه الله لمعنى وحكمة

rows.speaker: ابن عربي
rows.claim: Ibn Arabi says Khidr will appear with the Companions of the Cave when the Mahdi appears, be martyred, and rank among the best martyrs in the Mahdi's army.
rows.anchor: أنه يظهر مع أصحاب الكهف في آخر الزمان عند ظهور المهدي ويستشهد

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن سفيان
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Sufyan says the man whom the Dajjal kills and revives in a report at the end of Sahih Muslim is Khidr.
rows.anchor: قال إبراهيم بن سفيان صاحب مسلم يقال : إن هذا الرجل هو الخضر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Khidr and Ilyas meet each year during pilgrimage season, shave one another's heads, and recite a supplication said to protect its reader from calamities and harmful creatures.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما يلتقي الخضر والياس في كل عام في الموسم

rows.speaker: أحمد
rows.claim: Ahmad's Zuhd adds that Khidr and Ilyas fast Ramadan in Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: وزاد أحمد في الزهد أنهما يصومان رمضان في بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says Khidr lives in Jerusalem between the Gate of Mercy and the Gate of the Tribes.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه مسكن الخضر بيت المقدس فيما بين باب الرحمة إلى باب الأسباط

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani reads Khidr as a figure for spiritual expansion and Ilyas for contraction, and raises the question whether the historical human Khidr lives on.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : الخضر كناية عن البسط والياس عن القبض

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum says all knowledge comes from God, but mediated instruction is not called ladunni; it is knowledge placed directly in the heart without an ordinary external means.
rows.anchor: قال في "بحر العلوم" : إنما قال من لدنا مع أن العلوم كلها من لدنه

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Bahr al-Ulum gives Umar, Ali, and disciplined saints as recipients of such knowledge, then cites sayings praising the breath of lovers and the worship of the ascetic.
rows.anchor: كما كان لعمر وعلي ولكثير من أولياء الله تعالى المرتاضين

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: He says such devoted, grateful people are few, cites the few grateful servants and people's lack of knowledge, and presents the Companions as exemplary guides.
rows.anchor: وقليل من عبادى الشكور

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya reading makes God's servant a free person released from servitude to other-than-God and chosen among the elect; mercy makes him receptive to divine attributes' light.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {فوجدا عبدا من عبادنآ}

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: In the Najmiyya reading, ladunni knowledge is knowledge of God's essence and attributes, which no one knows unless God teaches it.
rows.anchor: وهو علم معرفة ذاته وصفاته الذي لا يعلمه أحد إلا بتعليمه إياه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Knowledge learnable from people is not uniquely ladunni; the author cites God teaching David armor-making, which could also be learned from another teacher.
rows.anchor: فإن علم صنعة اللبوس مما علمه الله داود عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd defines ladunni knowledge as unambiguous disclosure of hidden realities through lights unveiled when a servant disciplines the limbs, abandons personal will, and stands before God without desire.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد قدس سره : العلم اللدني ما كان تحكما على الأسرار بغير ظن فيه ولا خلاف

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The author's shaykh says mercy is knowledge of worship, study, outward law, and sharia; its being from God means it comes from the level of divine attributes.
rows.anchor: المراد بالرحمة علم العبادة والدراسة والظاهر والشريعة ولذلك عبر عنه بالرحمة

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: He reads knowledge as inward allusion, inheritance, and truth, called knowledge because it is the fullest form; like spirit to body or kernel to shell, it completes rather than invalidates outward knowledge.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعلم علم الإشارة والوراثة والباطن والحقيقة ولذلك عبر عنه بلفظ العلم

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: He says outward and inward knowledge are each perfect in themselves; apparent inferiority or superiority exists only through comparison between levels, not in their essential reality.
rows.anchor: فكما أن الجهل والغفلة في أنفسهما محض نقصان حقيقي فكذلك العلم والمعرفة في أنفسهما محض كمال حقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse about God as First, Last, Manifest, and Hidden frames differences as arrangements of levels; in their essential perfection the levels form a circle without distinguishable ends.
rows.anchor: {هو الاول والاخر والظاهر والباطن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each of the four Sunni legal imams leads Sufis of his school; like the four caliphs and celestial lights, following any one guides the seeker, while guidance to paradise and vision requires following their path.
rows.anchor: ورئيس أهل الذكر الصوفية الحنفية هو الإمام الأعظم الأكمل ورئيس أهل الذكر الصوفية الشافعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following an imam in law, spiritual path, truth, knowledge, conduct, and manners is following the Messenger; abandoning them leads away from his path and acceptance.
rows.anchor: ومن اقتدى بهم في الشريعة والطريقة والحقيقة وعلم علومهم وعمل أعمالهم وتأدب بآدابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects claims that the independent jurists did not attain divine love as utterances from spiritual intoxication, advising respectful silence about them.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنها كلمات صدرت حالة السكر والغلبات فلا اعتبار بها والأدب التام أن يمسك عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks to accompany Khidr for instruction in knowledge that guides him toward good; the question follows naturally from their meeting.
rows.anchor: استئذان منه في اتباعه له على وجه التعليم ويكفيك دليلا في شرف الاتباع

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses guidance as knowledge grounded in right direction, meaning attainment of good.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (علمي كه مبني بررشد باشد)

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam reads Moses's request as exemplary humility: he makes himself a follower, asks permission, admits his own need and the teacher's knowledge, seeks only a portion, and asks for guidance he lacks.
rows.anchor: الآية تدل على أن موسى راعى أنواع الأدب جعل نفسه تبعا له

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says even Moses, God's chosen interlocutor, did not consider himself satisfied with his knowledge but sought instruction.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : لو كان أحد مكتفيا من العلم لاكتفى نجي الله موسى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Moses's quest shows no one should abandon learning, even after reaching the highest level; a saying urges seeking knowledge from cradle to grave.
rows.anchor: وفيما فعل موسى وهو من أجلة الأنبياء من طلب العلم والرحلة في ذلك

rows.speaker: العلماء
rows.claim: Scholars say Moses's prophetic office and law do not prevent him learning another prophet's hidden sciences that do not concern his own legal rulings.
rows.anchor: ولا ينافي نبوة موسى وكونه صاحب شريعة أن يتعلم من نبي آخر

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The shaykh calls Khidr's teaching a complete one's instruction of a more complete one: God may reveal secrets to the former and then use him as a means to teach the latter without changing their ranks.
rows.anchor: تعليم موسى وتربيته بالخضر إنما هو من قبيل تعليم الأكمل وتربيته بالكامل

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The shaykh says outward and inward knowledge exist in both prophets, differing mainly by which dominates each nature; the Messenger is nevertheless, by consensus, the most knowledgeable and best of creation.
rows.anchor: وإلا فالعلم الظاهر والباطن حاصلان في نشأة كل منهما

rows.speaker: قصص الأنبياء
rows.claim: A story compares human knowledge with a bird's tiny dip of its beak from the sea: that is all humanity has received.
rows.anchor: وفي قصص الأنبياء بينما هما على ساحل البحر إذ أقبل طائر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A sincere disciple should ask the shaykh's permission to follow and remain in his company with humility, leaving home, status, supporters, and friends as Moses did.
rows.anchor: من آداب المريد الصادق بعد طلب الشيخ ووجدانه أن يستجيز منه في اتباعه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The reading calls direct divine illumination a higher kind of guidance than revelation through Gabriel, a book, or speech, interpreting Moses's request as seeking an unmediated light beyond duality.
rows.anchor: الرشد الحقيقي من الله للعبد هو أن يجعله قابلا لفيض نور الله بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A disciple serving a realized shaykh should put aside pride in ancestry, reputation, position, virtues, and knowledge, regard himself as ignorant, and obey the shaykh's commands.
rows.anchor: ينبغي أن يخرج عما معه من الحسب والنسب والجاه والمنصب والفضائل والعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr emphatically denies that Moses can endure with him; denying ability entails denying patience, and the passage suggests ability accompanies the act.
rows.anchor: نفى عنه استطاعة الصبر معه على وجه التأكيد كأنه مما لا يصح ولا يستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr explains that Moses cannot be patient with unfamiliar acts because their outward appearance will seem wrong to a righteous lawgiver, who will naturally object.
rows.anchor: وهو إيذان بأنه يتولى أمورا خفية منكرة الظواهر

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says a well-trained student may struggle most when learning from someone more complete: habitual disputation makes the student judge by appearances, argue, and alienate the teacher.
rows.anchor: الأول إذا وصل إلى من هو أكمل منه عسر عليه التعلم جدا

rows.speaker: شيخي وسندي
rows.claim: The shaykh says both prophets possess outward and inward knowledge, but outward knowledge dominates Moses and inward knowledge Khidr; Khidr predicts difficulty because the dominant mode governs each encounter.
rows.anchor: الغالب في نشأة موسى هو العلم الظاهري كما يدل عليه رسالته

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A sincere disciple remains at the shaykh's door despite repeated refusals meant to test his sincerity, as Moses persists after Khidr warns him.
rows.anchor: ومن الآداب أن يكون المريد ثابتا في الإرادة بحيث لو يرده الشيخ كرات بعد مرات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The inward reading contrasts Moses, judging by revealed outward law, with Khidr, acting by unveiled inward command; Khidr says he knows and acts only through God's identity and power.
rows.anchor: ومذهبي أن أحكم بالباطن على ما أمرني الله من العلم اللدني وقد كوشفت بحقائق الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promises patience without objection if God wills; invoking the will asks for help, seeks blessing, or acknowledges how hard patience will be.
rows.anchor: وتعليق الوعد بالمشيئة إما طلبا لتوفيقه في الصبر ومعونته أو تيمنا به

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some say Moses qualified his promise because he was not certain he could keep it; this is customary among the righteous.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنما استثنى لأنه لم يكن على ثقة فيما التزم من الصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author repeats a saying that all prophets had a phlegmatic temperament except Moses, whose temperament was bilious.
rows.anchor: ويقال إن أمزجة جميع الأنبياء البلغم إلا موسى فإن مزاجه كان المرة

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some explain that Moses spoke as a learner who needed explanations and therefore objected, while Ishmael was already in a posture of surrender and patience.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العلماء لأن موسى جاء صحبة الخضر بصورة التعلم والمتعلم لا يصبر

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view says Moses occupied a state of protective zeal and quickness, whereas the intended sacrifice occupied a state of judgment and patience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كان في مقام الغيرة والحدة والذبيح في مقام الحكم والصبر

rows.speaker: بعض العارفين
rows.claim: Some gnostics say Ishmael joined the patient community and succeeded, while Moses singled himself out as patient and failed; surrender rather than self-assertion best attains the station.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العارفين قال الذبيح من الصابرين أدخل نفسه في عداد الصابرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise not to disobey is coordinated with the promise to be patient; its eventual failure makes the original pledge rhetorically emphatic.
rows.anchor: وفي عدم هذا الوجدان من المبالغة ما ليس في الوعد بنفس الصبر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A disciple should not object to a shaykh's actions, words, or states; even when something seems contrary to reason or law, he should assume his own insight is deficient.
rows.anchor: أن لا يكون معترضا على أفعال الشيخ وأقواله وأحواله وجميع حركاته وسكناته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr permits Moses to follow on the condition that he not question any action he finds objectionable until Khidr explains it; this is learner etiquette and assumes each act has a good purpose.
rows.anchor: لا تفاتحني بالسؤال عن حكمته فضلا عن المناقشة والاعتراض

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The disciple should close the door to questions and wait for the shaykh to explain through words or through a state.
rows.anchor: ومن الآداب أن يسد على نفسه باب السؤال فلا يسأل الشيخ عن شيء حتى يحدث له منه ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman saw David making armor and restrained himself from asking about it; after David finished and wore it, he explained that it was excellent armor.
rows.anchor: دخل على داود عليه السلام وهو يسرد دروعا ولم يكن رآها قبل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says Luqman visited David for a year wanting to ask, but stayed silent.
rows.anchor: كان يتردد إليه سنة وهو يريد أن يسأل ذلك فلم يسأل

rows.speaker: الحكماء
rows.claim: The sages say speech is silver but silence is gold.
rows.anchor: قالت الحكماء إن كان الكلام من فضة فالصمت من ذهب

rows.speaker: بعض الكبار
rows.claim: Some elders distinguish silence of the tongue from idle talk, silence of the heart from worldly thoughts, and say combining both opens the servant's secret and unveils the Lord.
rows.anchor: ومن صمت لسانه وقلبه ظهر له سره وتجلى له ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wise should quiet inner resistance and verbal protest, forget all besides God, endure where patience is called for, and surrender because every event has wisdom and every loss compensation.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد حتى يسلم قلبه من الانقباض ولسانه من الاعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Khidr went along the coast seeking a ship. Although one report says Moses sent Joshua back to Israel, the author favors Kashifi's view that Joshua followed behind them.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير وهو الظاهر فإن تثنية الفعل إنما هي لأجل الانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rakiba fi describes entering a moving vessel, with fi highlighting the ship as the space entered, unlike riding a horse.
rows.anchor: وإن استعمل في الثاني يلوح بمحلية المفعول بكلمة في فيقال ركبت في السفينة

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn glosses the phrase as riding the sea in a ship.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : {حتى إذا ركبا} البحر {فى السفينة}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boatmen recognized Khidr and carried Moses and Khidr without a fare.
rows.anchor: فعرفوا الخضر فحملوهما بغير نول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr secretly pried two boards loose with an axe at deep water; Moses plugged the hole with his clothes, while Khidr is said to have patched it with glass or a rag.
rows.anchor: حيث أخذ فأسا فقلع بغتة أي : على غفلة من القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the boat did not begin taking in water after Khidr damaged it.
rows.anchor: روي أنه لما خرق السفينة لم يدخلها الماء

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam says Khidr apparently damaged the hull enough to show a defect, but not so much that its owners would immediately drown.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه خرق جدارها لتكون ظاهرة العيب ولا يتسارع إلى أهلها الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses objects that the hole could drown the people, who had kindly carried them for free, so damaging their boat seemed an unjust return.
rows.anchor: فإن خرقها سبب لدخول الماء فيها المفضي إلى غرق أهلها وهم قد أحسنوا بنا

rows.speaker: سعدي المفتي
rows.claim: Saadi says the lām is purposive rather than consequential, which better fits Moses's reproach.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يحمل على التعليل بل هو الأنسب لمقام الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imran means an astonishing, shocking, or strange deed; Zamakhshari's rhetorical example repeats amran in a wordplay about time's unusual events.
rows.anchor: أمر أمر منكر عجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr's reminder that Moses cannot be patient recalls his warning and reproaches Moses for failing to keep his promise.
rows.anchor: وهو تذكير لما قاله من قبل متضمن للإنكار على عدم الوفاء بوعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says he forgot the instruction not to ask about an action before its explanation; the author cites Bukhari distinguishing the first lapse as forgetfulness, the second as excess, and the third as deliberate.
rows.anchor: من أن الأول كان من موسى نسيانا والثاني فرطا والثالث عمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahq can mean to cover, burden, or force someone to bear what he cannot; Moses asks Khidr not to make following him difficult.
rows.anchor: والإرهاق أن يحمل الإنسان على ما لا يطيقه وأرهقه عشرا كلفه إياه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the request as do not cause me harm.
rows.anchor: ولا تغشني ولا تكلفني ولا تحملني

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A shaykh should test rather than eagerly accept a disciple, warning of the path's difficulty; once the disciple proves sincere and turns from all else, the shaykh should welcome and nurture him.
rows.anchor: ومن آداب الشيخ وشرائطه في الشيخوخة أن لا يحرص على قبول المريد بل يمتحنه

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The shaykh should overlook many slips from a weak disciple, but correct violations of commands or prohibitions and objections to the shaykh; after repentance, confession, and a pledge not to repeat them, accept his apology.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن يتغافل عن كثير من زلات المريد رحمة عليه ولا يؤاخذه بكل سهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asks not to be burdened beyond his capacity; the verse openly shows that prophets can forget, and an accompanied apology makes a lapse still less blameworthy.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية تصريح بأن النسيان يعتري الأنبياء عليهم السلام للإشعار بأن غيره تعالى معيوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem advises accepting the excuses of someone who apologizes, whether the explanation is true or false.
rows.anchor: أقبل معاذير من يأتيك معتذرا إن بر عندك فيما قال أو فجرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God and His saints impose severe tests, so the seeker must be patient, surrender, and accept what comes.
rows.anchor: ثم إن امتحان الله وامتحان أوليائه شديد فلا بد من الصبر والتسليم والرضى

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن خفيف
rows.claim: Ibn Khafif relates that after forty days without food and avoiding Junayd, he saw a gazelle drink from a well; when he approached, it fled and the water fell out of reach.
rows.anchor: وعن الشيخ أبي عبد الله بن خفيف قدس سره قال : دخلت بغداد قاصدا الحج

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن خفيف
rows.claim: A voice told Ibn Khafif he had been tested and failed to endure; unlike the gazelle, he had brought a bucket and rope. Returning, he found the well full and had water through his pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: جربناك فلم تصبر ارجع فخذ الماء إن الظبي جاء بلا ركوة ولا حبل

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: When Ibn Khafif returned from pilgrimage, Junayd said patience for one hour would have made water spring from beneath his feet.
rows.anchor: لو صبرت لنبع الماء من تحت قدمك لو صبرت صبر ساعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Khidr accepts Moses's apology, they leave the boat and meet a youth outside a village; Khidr kills him by grasping and pulling off his head, as the sound report from Ubayy ibn Ka'b says.
rows.anchor: ومعنى قتله أشار بأصابعه الثلاث الإبهام والسبابة والوسطة

rows.speaker: السهيلي
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli gives the slain boy's name in variant forms: Jaysur, Haysur, or Haynun.
rows.anchor: واسمه جيسور بالجيم أو حيسور بالحاء أو حينون قاله السهيلي

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most say zakiyya means pure and sinless because the boy was a minor who had not reached accountability.
rows.anchor: طاهرة من الذنوب لأنها صغيرة لم تبلغ الحنث

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, and Abu Amr read zakiyya; the other readers read zakiyya with a doubled z, and Abu Amr distinguishes never-sinning from one who sinned then repented.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو زاكية والباقون زكية فعيلة للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without a life means the boy had not killed anyone, so there was no retaliatory ground for killing him.
rows.anchor: بغير قتل نفس محرمة يعني لم تقتل نفسا فيقتص منها

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer the boy was older because a minor cannot be subject to retaliation; they reply that legal rulings differed and perhaps a child could be killed under Khidr's law.
rows.anchor: قيل الصغير لا يقاد فالظاهر من الآية كبر الغلام وفيه أن الشرائع مختلفة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqi says legal duties became tied to puberty after the Hijra; Taqi al-Din al-Subki places that change after Uhud.
rows.anchor: ما نقل البيهقي في "كتاب المعرفة" أن الأحكام إنما صارت متعلقة بالبلوغ بعد الهجرة

rows.speaker: صاحب إنسان العيون
rows.claim: Insan al-Uyun cites Ali's own verse saying he preceded others in Islam as a child before puberty, then says children were responsible then and exemption began at Khaybar.
rows.anchor: سبقتكمو إلى الإسلام طرا صغيرا ما بلغت أوان حلمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse singles out absence of a prior killing because that is the most likely excuse given the boy's age; a report says the boy was destined to be an unbeliever.
rows.anchor: لأنه أقرب إلى الوقوع نظرا إلى حال الغلام

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi says the boy was treated as Muslim because his parents were believers; the report that he was branded an unbeliever means that, if he lived, he would have become one.
rows.anchor: قال النووي لما كان أبواه مؤمنين كان هو مؤمنا أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nukran is more shocking than imran because the ship's damage could be repaired, while killing the boy could not be undone.
rows.anchor: لأن ذلك كان خرقا يمكن تداركه بالسد وهذا لا سبيل إلى تداركه

rows.speaker: جماعة من القراء
rows.claim: Some Quran reciters mark the halfway point of the Quran at this verse.
rows.anchor: قال جماعة من القراء نصف القرآن

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: An alternative view says the murder was less grave than the risk of drowning all the boat's passengers.
rows.anchor: وقيل الأمر أعظم من النكر لأن قتل نفس واحدة أهون من إغراق أهل السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr adds laka, you, to his reminder to intensify the reproach because Moses has now broken his promise twice.
rows.anchor: وزيادة لك هنا لزيادة العتاب على تركها لأنه قد نقض العهد مرتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses says that if he asks again, Khidr may end their companionship; after three violations Khidr will have an excuse to leave him.
rows.anchor: قد وجدت عذرا من قبلي لما خالفتك ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An excuse is an attempt to erase the trace of a sin; repentance is one form of excuse, though not every excuse is repentance, and the root suggests cutting off resentment.
rows.anchor: والاعتذار عبارة عن محو أثر الذنب وأصله القطع

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed for mercy for Moses and said that had Moses stayed with Khidr, they would have seen more wonders.
rows.anchor: رحم الله أخي موسى استحيى فقال ذلك لو لبث مع صاحبه لأبصر أعجب الأعاجيب

rows.speaker: صاحب الخصائص الصغرى
rows.claim: Al-Khasa'is al-Sughra says Muhammad alone combined law and inward truth, while most prophets judged by outward matters and Khidr by inward realities; neither prophet was commanded to use the other's knowledge.
rows.anchor: ومن خصائصه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه جمعت له الشريعة والحقيقة ولم يكن للأنبياء إلا أحدهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The village is identified as Antioch, a regional capital with many springs, a great stone wall, five mountains inside it, and a circuit of twelve miles.
rows.anchor: هي أنطاكية بالفتح والكسر وسكون النون وكسر الكاف وفتح الياء المخففة قاعدة العواصم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the village gates were shut at night; Moses and Khidr arrived hungry, asked to enter and for food, but the people refused them.
rows.anchor: نماز شام موسى وخضر بدان ديه رسيدند وخواستندكه بديه در آيند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They asked the residents for food; another view says they did not ask directly, but merely lodging among the people amounted to asking hospitality.
rows.anchor: ولكن نزولهما عندهم كالسؤال منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase makes the request a description of the village, not merely its people, intensifying the blame: residents who refused hospitality in their own home acted especially badly.
rows.anchor: لزيادة تشنيعهم على سوء صنيعهم فإن الإباء من الضيافة وهم أهلها قاطنون بها أقبح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question contrasts Moses's rejected request here with his help to Shuayb's daughters; the author says he relied on God at Midian but here leaned on created provision instead of God.
rows.anchor: إن الحرمان كان بسبب المعارضة بحيث لم يكتف بعلم الله بحاله بل جنح إلى الاعتماد على مخلوق

rows.speaker: سعدي
rows.claim: Saadi's verses praise travelers who spread a good name, urging people to welcome strangers and protect them from harm.
rows.anchor: بزر كان مسافر بجان رورند كه نام نكويى بعالم برند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says villagers offered the Prophet gold if he would change the letter fa in the verse to ta, making it say they came to host the guests; he refused because that would falsify God's speech.
rows.anchor: نشتري بهذا أن تجعل الباء تاء يعني فأتوا أن يضيفوهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kashifi says Moses and Khidr left hungry at dawn, resumed their route, and found a leaning wall near the village.
rows.anchor: إيشان كرسنه بيرون ديه بودند بامداد روى براه نهادند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the wall willing to collapse is an Arabic metaphor: a wall has no will, but was close to falling; al-Irshad says the wording stresses imminent collapse.
rows.anchor: والإرادة من الله هي الحكم وهذا من مجاز كلام العرب لأن الجدار لا إرادة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inqidad means falling rapidly; the lexicographers derive it either from the verb for breaking or from a form expressing rapid descent.
rows.anchor: والانقضاض الإسراع في السقوط وهو انفعال من القض

rows.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says Khidr righted the wall with a gesture of his hand; it was a hundred cubits high.
rows.anchor: فسواه الخضر بالإشارة بيده كما هو المروي عن النبي عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says Moses explained that the villagers had given them neither lodging nor food, then asked why Khidr had repaired their wall.
rows.anchor: كفت موسى اين أهل ديه مارا جاى ندادند وطعام نيز نفرستادند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses suggests Khidr could have taken a wage for the work so they could buy food.
rows.anchor: أجرة حتى نشتري بها طعاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittakhadha is the form iftaala meaning took; according to Basran grammarians it is not derived directly from akhdh.
rows.anchor: افتعل من اتخذ بمعنى أخذ كأتبع وليس من الأخذ عند البصريين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some recount Khidr's witty replies: Moses was in the sea without drowning, killed an Egyptian without cause, and forgot to water Shuayb's daughters without payment.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم لما قال له {لتغرق أهلها} قال الخضر : أليس كنت في البحر ولم تغرق من غير سفينة

rows.speaker: القاسم
rows.claim: Al-Qasim says a gazelle stood between the hungry travelers: it was unroasted on Moses's side and roasted on Khidr's, reflecting Khidr's disinterest and Moses's turn toward gain.
rows.anchor: وقف ظبي بينهما وهما جائعان من جانب موسى غير مشوي ومن جانب الخضر مشوي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says noticing one's work and seeking its reward invalidates the work, citing Moses's wage suggestion before separation.
rows.anchor: رؤية العمل وطلب الثواب به يبطل العمل ألا ترى الكليم لما قال للخضر

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd says the darkness of desire veils the heart from seeing the inward wisdom of divine acts.
rows.anchor: إذا وردت ظلمة الاطماع على القلوب حجبت النفوس على نظرها في بواطن الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Moses focused on the benefit to the wall's owners, not labor or miracle; compensation for ruqya such as recitation of the Opening is allowed, but a prophet may not charge for preaching and guidance.
rows.anchor: إنه جوز أخذ الأجر بمقالة الرقية بسورة الفاتحة ونحوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khidr says this is the moment of separation; the third objection triggers the parting he had promised after another question.
rows.anchor: هذا الوقت وقت الفراق بيننا وهذا الاعتراض الثالث سبب الفراق الموعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase between me and you uses the verbal noun separation with its following adverbial in an expanded construction.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الفراق إلى البين إضافة المصدر إلى الظرف اتساعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle in I shall inform emphasizes certainty rather than delay.
rows.anchor: السين للتأكيد لعدم تراخي التنبئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ta'wil here means the outcome: the boat's rescue from seizure, the parents' rescue from the boy with a better replacement, and the orphans' recovery of the treasure.
rows.anchor: والمراد به ههنا المآل والعاقبة إذ هو المنبأ به دون التأويل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said they wished Moses had remained patient so God could tell them more of the pair's story through revelation.
rows.anchor: وددنا أن موسى كان صبر حتى يقص علينا من خبرهما

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: A shaykh may forgive one or two objections, but after a third should part; before leaving, he should explain the hidden wisdom so the disciple does not depart still objecting.
rows.anchor: فإن عاد إلى الثالثة فلا يصاحبه لأنه قد بلغ من لدنه عذرا

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
rows.claim: Bayazid told a disobedient disciple that someone cast from God's sight would be ruined; the disciple later suffered public disgrace and theft, unlike a faithful disciple of Abu Sulayman who entered a fire and emerged unharmed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يزيد البسطامي قدس سره في حق تلميذه لما خالفه دعوا من سقط من عين الله
